title: Faster Science, Better Drugs

reader_summary.overview: Arbunchot is really to make virtual cells at ARC and simulate human biology, the foundation models. Why are we so worried about modeling entire bodies over time when we can't do it for an individual cell? We can figure out how to model the fundamental unit of biology, the cell, then from that we should be able to build.

thesis: The speakers argue that science is slow due to a complex knot of incentives, physical distance between disciplines, and a lack of collaboration, which the ARC Institute aims to solve by co-locating multiple fields under one roof. They propose making science faster by developing virtual cells and foundation models that allow experimentalists to iterate at the speed of neural network forward passes, though they acknowledge that biology is harder to model than language or images because humans do not natively understand biological tokens.
